attendees.role: school committee member (announced resignation effective May 16)

attendees.name_as_heard: Mr. Skulbrini (heard variously as "Scho brini"/"Scholbrini", called "Tony" by colleagues)

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the total warrant amount for the period covering line-item transfers.

budget_items.topic: Vehicle maintenance to contractor services transfer
budget_items.what_was_said: Dr. Gilson requested a transfer to cover HVAC unit repairs on the roof, after a committee member asked for more detail on what was being fixed.
A second transfer moving money from general supplies, ELL, ACE and mileage reimbursement lines into a contracted evaluation special education line was described but not voted this meeting.
The superintendent's report noted an unbudgeted cost presented to the finance committee for 911 compliance upgrades at Turkey Hill Elementary, now complete districtwide.
Dr. Gilson said current athletic fees offset only a portion of athletic expenses under FY24 numbers, and that the fund faces a growing deficit without a fee increase.
The committee voted to raise athletic fees for the first student, with a sibling discount, a reduced/waiver rate, and a family cap.
The athletic director's cost breakdown by season was read into the record for fall, winter and spring sports.
A per-sport cost figure for football was given, though the figure stated moments later was inconsistent with it.
A proposal to replace the flat activity fee with a lower base fee plus a special-interest club fee was presented for feedback, not a vote, citing a growing deficit in the activity account.
A proposal to charge a K-6 transportation fee (not legally required) at several possible daily rates was presented and tabled pending a parent survey.
The committee voted to raise custodian, kitchen and field monitor labor rates and increase facility rental fees roughly across the board.

budget_items.topic: FY26 budget gap and town manager's revised number
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager's revised budget figure was described as higher than originally expected but largely absorbed by a higher-than-budgeted health insurance increase, leaving a personnel-cut gap.
Administration compared annual Chapter 70 increases to inflation for three prior years to argue state aid is not keeping pace.

budget_items.topic: North Middlesex central office consolidation option
budget_items.what_was_said: A proposal to eliminate central office administrators and pay North Middlesex for shared time was estimated to produce savings, though not adopted.
A proposal to eliminate the director of finance and administration position and add an accountant plus contracted HR support was discussed and tabled over continuity concerns.

budget_items.topic: Money available to restore cut positions
budget_items.what_was_said: Administration walked through cumulative dollars becoming available toward restoring positions, including expense cuts, a lower out-of-district tuition need, and the possible transportation fee.

Costs of educating certain out-of-district-eligible students in-district versus at Keystone Collaborative or North Middlesex were compared; staying in-district was said to be cheapest and best for students.

budget_items.topic: Federal special education and title grants
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff described how IDEA and Title I/IIA/IVA grant funds are targeted, mostly paying for paraprofessionals and coaching/mentoring rather than covering the deficit.

decisions.decision: Tabled the bus transportation fee proposal for further discussion, pending a parent survey and more data.
Tabled the student activity fee restructuring proposal and agreed to seek student council feedback before acting.
Tabled cuts to middle school/freshman athletic coaches and uniform replacement, pending a recommendation from the athletic director on which sports could be cut.
Tabled the proposal to eliminate the director of finance and administration position, citing continuity-of-operations concerns with an incoming new superintendent.
Gave direction to proceed with hiring the previously interviewed candidate for facilities/grounds director rather than leaving it vacant or merging with the town.
Agreed to pursue a joint meeting with the select board tentatively on March 11.
Agreed to proceed with the MASC-recommended superintendent search timeline, with the possibility of the search committee proceeding with 11 rather than 12 members due to a scheduling conflict.
Mr. Beardmore announced he will resign from the school committee effective May 16, creating a third vacancy on the ballot.
Set March 11 as the date for a joint meeting with the select board given the March 17 warrant deadline.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee spent most of a long meeting confronting a severe FY26 budget shortfall driven by inflation, rising special education and transportation costs, and state Chapter 70 aid not keeping pace, with public and committee comment repeatedly blaming inadequate state funding and past reluctance to override. The committee voted to raise athletic fees and facility rental rates, tabled proposed transportation and student-activity fee changes, walked through a long menu of possible administrative, staffing and program cuts, and took public budget questions; a member also announced he will resign in May.

what_happened.line: The committee voted 5-0 to raise athletic user fees, adding a sibling discount, a reduced-fee tier, and a family cap.
The committee also voted 5-0 to raise facility rental fees and labor rates for custodial, kitchen, and field staff.
A proposed new bus transportation fee was tabled pending a parent survey and more ridership data.
A proposal to restructure student activity fees was tabled pending feedback from student council.
A committee member announced he will resign effective May 16, opening a third seat on the ballot.

why_it_matters: Higher athletic and facility rental fees land directly on families with student athletes and on anyone renting a school or town facility, separate from the tax levy.
The tabled transportation and activity-fee proposals remain live questions that could still change what families pay for busing and clubs.
The resignation adds a third open seat to the school committee ballot, at a time when the board is making the FY26 budget cuts.
